name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,781

entries.clue: One reluctant to join party with a large liberal elite (10)

blocks.note: L = large, as on clothing labels
the flower of a group is its elite

annotation.surface: A liberal elite at a big party, and somebody who would rather not join in.
annotation.walkthrough: "Party" here is a social gathering, not a political one, despite "liberal elite" pulling towards politics.
annotation.definitionFit: A wallflower hangs back at a dance or party rather than joining in.

entries.clue: The Killers or Stock, Aitken and Waterman, say (6)

blocks.note: contract killers, paid to carry out a hit
a trio of men who produced a string of chart hits

annotation.surface: A list of pop acts: the American band The Killers and the 1980s British hit-making production team.
annotation.walkthrough: The Killers are a rock band, so both halves look like pop trivia. Stock, Aitken and Waterman were a British trio who produced dozens of chart hits in the 1980s.
annotation.definitionFit: Killers-for-hire are hitmen, and men who churn out hits are, punningly, hit men.

entries.clue: A part of working? That's being cool-headed! (2,2)

indicatorNotes.headed: cool is put at the head, before working

blocks.note: a machine that is on is working

annotation.surface: Someone asking what part of a job needs, and answering: keeping a cool head.
annotation.walkthrough: "Cool-headed" reads as calm, but it is an instruction: cool (IN) heads working (ON).
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: being party to a secret or scheme is being a part of it.

entries.clue: Steal vehicle close to detective, but be cautious (4,4)

indicatorNotes.close to: the close of a word is its last letter

annotation.surface: A car thief being warned to watch out for the police.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is the verb phrase "be cautious"; "but" only joins it to the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: telling someone to watch out is telling them to be cautious.

entries.clue: More drugs that heartless lags will inject (4)

indicatorNotes.heartless: the heart of LAGS (AG) is removed
indicatorNotes.will inject: the drugs take LS inside them

blocks.note: E = ecstasy, twice for plural drugs
LAGS without its middle AG, placed between the two Es

annotation.surface: Prisoners injecting still more drugs.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface has the lags injecting; the wordplay reverses it, with the drugs taking in the lags.
annotation.definitionFit: "Anything else?" means "anything more?"

entries.clue: Out-of-head member of your clan in high spirits (7)

indicatorNotes.Out-of-head: the head, or first letter, is taken out

blocks.note: RELATION, a member of your family, without its first letter R

annotation.surface: A relative who is out of their head and very merry.
annotation.walkthrough: "Out-of-head" suggests someone drunk or high; it is a beheading instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: great joy and excitement amount to high spirits.

entries.clue: A place a stud might go around, getting disease (5)

indicatorNotes.go around: the letters go round, turning back to front

blocks.note: an earlobe, where a stud earring goes

annotation.surface: Someone's piercing turning into an infection.
annotation.walkthrough: A + LOBE turned round gives the answer; "go around" sounds like the stud going through the ear.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: a deadly haemorrhagic fever from central Africa is a disease.

entries.clue: Improvise brief defence to secure chess file (2-3)

indicatorNotes.brief: cut short, losing its last letter
indicatorNotes.to secure: to secure something is to hold it fast, so ALIB is wrapped round D

blocks.note: chessboard files are lettered a to h; the d-file is one

annotation.surface: A chess player thinking on their feet to protect a file.
annotation.walkthrough: In chess, a file is a column of the board, named by a letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, from Latin ad libitum, 'at pleasure': to speak without a script.

entries.clue: Knight in boozer with single noblewoman in Paris (7)

indicatorNotes.in: the knight goes in the single

blocks.note: a boozer is a pub, a bar
one = single; N goes inside to make ONNE

annotation.surface: A knight drinking in a pub with an unmarried French aristocrat.
annotation.walkthrough: "In Paris" flags a French word.
annotation.definitionFit: A foreign-language equivalent: the French feminine of baron, signalled by 'in Paris'.

entries.clue: Lie about spondulicks, not having any yen (4)

indicatorNotes.not having any: not having any yen means the money is left without its Y

blocks.note: spondulicks and lolly are both British slang for money
Y = yen, the Japanese currency; removed from LOLLY

annotation.surface: Someone lying about money, claiming to have no longing for it.
annotation.walkthrough: "Yen" also means a longing, so the surface reads as someone lying about not wanting money.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to lounge or sprawl lazily is to lie about.

entries.clue: Moon regent travelling around country abroad (10)

indicatorNotes.travelling around: letters that travel around do not stay in their order, so they are rearranged

annotation.surface: A ruler named Moon on a foreign tour.
annotation.walkthrough: "Moon" looks like a name, but its letters join REGENT to make the fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: Montenegro is a Balkan country, abroad from a British solver's point of view.

entries.clue: Naughty boys seizing northern infertile region (8)

indicatorNotes.seizing: BAD LADS grab N and hold it inside

annotation.surface: Delinquents taking over a barren stretch of the north.
annotation.walkthrough: Bad lads is British slang for tearaways or troublemakers.
annotation.definitionFit: Badlands are barren, eroded land where little grows.

entries.clue: Down? Flipping take too many drugs, Hoskins? (5)

annotation.definitionNote: Hoskins is the setter, mocking himself; the question mark flags the definition by example.

indicatorNotes.Flipping: turned over, so OD reads DO

annotation.surface: A mock-despairing question about whether the setter is depressed and overdoing it.
annotation.walkthrough: "Flipping" reads as a mild British swearword; it is a reversal instruction. A saddo is British slang for a pathetic, boring person.
annotation.definitionFit: The setter jokingly calls himself a saddo, a pathetic loser.

entries.clue: Laurel found in outskirts of Armenia's capital (6)

indicatorNotes.found in: to be found in a place is to be inside it, so STAN sits within the As
indicatorNotes.outskirts of: just the outer letters are used

blocks.note: first and last letters of ArmeniA
Stan Laurel, of Laurel and Hardy; goes between the two As

annotation.surface: A laurel tree growing on the edge of Yerevan.
annotation.walkthrough: "Armenia's capital" suggests Yerevan, but the capital is Kazakhstan's; Armenia only supplies its outer letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: the seat of government of Kazakhstan is a capital city.

entries.clue: Actor in rug belted about in comfortable motor (7,3)

indicatorNotes.belted about: bashed around, so the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: An actor in a toupee being beaten up in a plush car.
annotation.walkthrough: "Rug" is slang for a wig, which makes the surface comic.
annotation.definitionFit: A touring car is a roomy car built for long, comfortable journeys.

entries.clue: Once again understood leader must become adult (4)

indicatorNotes.leader must become: the first letter is swapped for another

blocks.note: A = adult (film rating); replaces the K

annotation.surface: Someone learning afresh that the boss has to grow up.
annotation.walkthrough: The leader of KNEW is its first letter, which must become A.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: afresh, starting over, means once again.

entries.clue: Foreign banker once more repelled artist (7)

indicatorNotes.repelled: driven back, so AGAIN is reversed

annotation.surface: An overseas banker driving off a painter a second time.
annotation.walkthrough: A "banker" in crosswords is often a river, something with banks; this one is in North America.
annotation.definitionFit: The Niagara is a river, a thing with banks, and it lies outside Britain.

entries.clue: Confuse Serpent mostly without fail ultimately (5)

indicatorNotes.mostly: most of a word, but not all, so the last letter is dropped
indicatorNotes.without: outside, so ADDE goes round L
indicatorNotes.ultimately: ultimately means in the end, so the end letter of fail is taken

blocks.note: ADDER, a snake, minus its last letter
last letter of faiL, placed inside ADDE

annotation.surface: An infallible snake bewildering someone.
annotation.walkthrough: "Without fail" reads as "always", but "without" here means outside.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to muddle someone's brain is to confuse them.

entries.clue: English queen hugged by American escort is ok (8)

indicatorNotes.hugged by: whatever is hugged is held in someone's arms, so EQU sits inside DATE

blocks.note: a date escorts you out; EQU goes after its D

annotation.surface: An English queen being cuddled by her American companion, who gets a so-so review.
annotation.walkthrough: QU for queen is a standard abbreviation; "is" only links the wordplay to "ok".
annotation.definitionFit: Adequate means ok, good enough.

entries.clue: One person exploiting another one taking horse? (4)

blocks.note: someone who exploits other people for their own ends
horse is slang for heroin, so this is a drug taker

annotation.surface: Someone taking advantage of another by making off with their horse.
annotation.walkthrough: "Horse" is drug slang for heroin, which the question mark flags.
annotation.definitionFit: A user is both an exploiter of others and a drug taker.

entries.clue: King meets a bishop, one with European girl's name (6)

blocks.note: K = king, in chess and cards
RR = Right Reverend, a bishop's title

annotation.surface: A king and a bishop meeting someone who has a European girl's name.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads "European girl's name" as one phrase; European only supplies E.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: a spelling of the name Carrie is a girl's name.

entries.clue: Golden one in European department's made a minister (8)

indicatorNotes.in: one being in something means it sits inside, so I goes into DANE

blocks.note: a Dane is a European; I goes inside to make DAINE

annotation.surface: A star member of a European department being given a ministerial post.
annotation.walkthrough: "Minister" suggests government, but a minister is also a member of the clergy.
annotation.definitionFit: A religious sense: being admitted to holy orders is being made a minister.

entries.clue: Strip of Dundee requiring some alterations (6)

indicatorNotes.requiring some alterations: the letters of DUNDEE need rearranging

annotation.surface: A strip of land in the Scottish city of Dundee needing building work.
annotation.walkthrough: "Strip" reads as a noun in the surface but is the verb.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to lay bare, removing every covering, is to strip.

entries.clue: One aids evacuation of soldiers up in eastern area (5)

indicatorNotes.up: in a down clue, up turns MEN over
indicatorNotes.in: the reversed soldiers are placed in the eastern area, inside E and A

annotation.surface: A military evacuation of troops from an eastern region.
annotation.walkthrough: The evacuation is of the bowels, not of troops.
annotation.definitionFit: An enema helps empty the bowels.

entries.clue: I am a gruff bleeding northern guttersnipe (10)

indicatorNotes.bleeding: damaged, so the letters are mixed up

annotation.surface: A rough street kid from the north introducing himself with a swearword.
annotation.walkthrough: "Bleeding" is a mild British swearword, which disguises it as an anagram indicator.
annotation.definitionFit: A ragamuffin is a scruffy street child, a guttersnipe.

entries.clue: Early man found by academician on embankment? (4)

blocks.note: DAM, a barrier across a river

annotation.surface: A caveman discovered by a scholar on a riverbank.
annotation.walkthrough: In a down clue, "on" puts A above DAM.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the Bible's first human is the earliest man of all.

entries.clue: Pretty-looking female with wind (4)

annotation.surface: An attractive woman with flatulence.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface's wind is the bodily kind; the wordplay wants plain moving air.
annotation.definitionFit: Fair means beautiful, pretty to look at.

entries.clue: Passes work with eager singletons primarily (4)

indicatorNotes.primarily: only the first letters are used

blocks.note: to work, of a machine, is to go

annotation.surface: A dating-app job that keeps keen single people busy.
annotation.walkthrough: Singletons are single people; only their first letter joins with that of eager.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: time that elapses passes, or moves on.

entries.clue: Flipping Dada paintings in a class of their own? (5)

annotation.definition: in a class of their own

indicatorNotes.Flipping: turned over, so PA reads AP

blocks.note: dada and pa both mean father

annotation.surface: Dadaist paintings praised as unique.
annotation.walkthrough: Dada was an art movement, which the surface leans on; here it is a child's word for father.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: something set aside from all others is in a class of its own.

entries.clue: Hot articles Hoskins had knocked over in state (7)

indicatorNotes.knocked over: turned over, so ANAID reads DIANA

blocks.note: the setter refers to himself: I

annotation.surface: The setter having knocked over some hot items somewhere.
annotation.walkthrough: Setters often refer to themselves by name, so Hoskins gives I; "had" gives D as in I'd.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: a Midwestern US state.
